articles.originalTitle: The universe has plenty of hydrogen. So why is star formation collapsing?
articles.excerpt: Star formation across the universe has fallen dramatically over the past 4.5 billion years, but astronomers have uncovered a surprising twist: the supply of neutral hydrogen, a key ingredient for making stars, has barely declined.
